items.title: NATO chief Rutte meets Trump amid US threat to leave alliance

featured_image.name: Trump is expected to meet with Rutte as he muses about pulling out ...

items.description:
NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte arrived at the White House on Wednesday for what may be the most consequential meeting in the alliance's 77-year history, as President Donald Trump's threats to withdraw the United States from the military bloc have plunged transatlantic relations into uncharted territory.

The meeting, confirmed by NATO and the Associated Press, comes after Trump told Reuters and The Telegraph in recent interviews that he is "absolutely" considering pulling the US out of NATO, citing what he called "disgust" with the alliance over European members' refusal to support the US-Israeli air campaign against Iran, launched on February 28. "I was never swayed by NATO," Trump said. "I always knew they were a paper tiger, and Putin knows that too, by the way."[1][2]

items.title: Vance to lead US delegation in Iran talks in Islamabad

featured_image.name: US Vice President Vance spoke to intermediaries about Iran ...

items.description: The United States and Iran are preparing for their first face-to-face negotiations since the outbreak of war, with Vice President JD Vance set to lead the American delegation to Islamabad this weekend for talks aimed at forging a lasting peace agreement. Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf will head Tehran's team, according to Iran's semi-official ISNA news agency. The high-stakes diplomacy follows a two-week ceasefire agreed to on Tuesday night, brokered largely through Pakistan's mediation.[1][2]

items.title: Trump sends Vance, Witkoff, Kushner to Islamabad for Iran talks

featured_image.name: Iran War Latest: Vance, Witkoff, Kushner Heading to Pakistan for Peace  Talks - Bloomberg

items.description:
President Donald Trump is dispatching a high-level delegation led by Vice President JD Vance to Islamabad for face-to-face negotiations with Iran, the White House announced Wednesday, just hours after a fragile two-week ceasefire halted 38 days of U.S. and Israeli military operations against Tehran.

White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt confirmed the team. "I can announce that the president is dispatching his negotiating team, led by the vice president of the United States, JD Vance, Special Envoy Witkoff and Mr. Kushner to Islamabad for talks this weekend," she said. "The first round of those talks will take place on Saturday morning local time."[1]

items.title: Israel learned of Iran cease-fire deal at last minute

featured_image.name: Netanyahu says announcement of Gaza ceasefire's next phase is ...

items.description:
Israel was not formally part of the negotiations that produced the two-week cease-fire between the United States and Iran announced on Tuesday, and Israeli officials were unhappy to learn that a deal had been finalized without prior consultation, according to a Wall Street Journal exclusive report citing mediators and a person familiar with the matter.[1]

The extent of Israel's involvement amounted to a phone call from President Donald Trump to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu shortly before the cease-fire was publicly announced, a White House official told the Journal. Netanyahu agreed to participate in the cease-fire during that call.[1]
